title: twr — Agent-first X/Twitter CLI (root epic)
description: Root epic tracking the full Rust port of public-clis/twitter-cli (Python, cookie-authenticated GraphQL) into 'twr': a CLI built agent-first (stable exit codes, JSON/YAML/TOON envelope, --dry-run/--apply/--policy safety, idempotency) with human table output as a thin view layer. Full design doc: COMPREHENSIVEPLANFORTWITTERCLI.md at repo root — every bead below embeds enough of that doc's content to be actionable without re-reading it, but the doc remains the canonical source if a bead's summary and the doc ever disagree. Thesis (plan §0): agent-first, human second — every decision prioritizes machine-parseability, then agent safety (policy/dry-run/idempotency), then human readability. NON-GOALS (plan §11, must never be violated by any child bead): twr does NOT do LLM summarization, newsworthiness ranking beyond the §7 engagement-score filter, scheduling/cron, or approval workflows beyond --apply/--dry-run/prompt — those are an external orchestrator's job, calling twr as a subprocess or MCP tool. Phases: P0 (viability spike, go/no-go gate) -> P1 (read MVP + full agent contract) -> P2 (writes + media + safety) -> P3 (human polish + SKILL/SCHEMA + release, partially already done) -> P4 (official API v2 backend, feature-gated) -> P5 (extras: SQLite cache, expanded doctor, schedule, guest-tier, MCP server).

title: GUARDRAIL: keep summarization/scheduling/approval logic OUT of twr
description: Standing reminder derived from plan §11 (Non-goals). twr is a safe read/write PRIMITIVE for X/Twitter — structured reads (feed/search/bookmarks/user/list -> JSON/YAML/TOON) and gated writes (post/reply/... with --dry-run/--apply/idempotency). It must never grow: (a) LLM calls / summarization, (b) newsworthiness ranking beyond the plain engagement-score --filter in twr-filter, (c) a daemon/cron/scheduler (the P5 future/schedule idea is a one-shot delay, NOT a cron replacement), (d) approval workflows beyond the --apply/--dry-run/TTY-prompt mechanics already specified in plan §5.3. Rationale: the moment twr makes editorial decisions it stops being a reusable primitive that any orchestrator (a daily-digest bot today, a completely different workflow tomorrow) can build on, and becomes a single-purpose bot. Any bead or PR that proposes adding one of these belongs in a SEPARATE downstream project, not this repo. Re-check this bead whenever scope creep is suspected; it should stay open indefinitely as a living checklist, not get closed.

title: Phase P0 — Viability spike (go/no-go gate)
description: Plan §9 P0. Answers exactly one question before any of the 15-module port begins: can Rust realistically reproduce an authenticated, browser-like request to X's internal GraphQL surface? Covers: wreq TLS-impersonation request success rate against x.com, rookie cookie extraction on Windows/Linux/macOS (Windows is the highest documented risk — upstream issue #28: Chrome DB lock + AES-GCM failures on Chrome>=127 + misleading diagnostics), a full port of the x-client-transaction-id derivation algorithm (agentic-x/transaction.py) with parity-tested vectors, and one end-to-end UserByScreenName call combining all three. If this phase fails, STOP — do not proceed to P1. Duration target: 1-2 days, deliberately kept narrow (do not expand scope here; that was reviewed and rejected in an earlier plan iteration — see the plan's own note that P0 must answer one question, not become P0.5 of the real port).
acceptance_criteria: P0_5 closed with an explicit GO decision recorded in its close_reason; NO-GO must halt all P1 work until a revised approach is agreed.

title: P0: wreq transport viability spike vs x.com
description: Build a minimal WreqTransport (crates/twr-client) using wreq's Emulation::Chrome13x against real x.com endpoints (not a mock). Measure request success rate (200s vs 403/999/blocked) for a handful of representative calls with real browser-exported cookies. This is the crate's central risk per plan §3: 'never reqwest, always browser-compatible transport fingerprinting via a trait, wreq is the default impl not an architectural dependency.' Acceptance: document the observed success rate and any blocking signatures seen; if wreq is fingerprinted and blocked, the plan's documented fallback is the curl-impersonate subprocess transport (plan §11 risk #3) — note whether that fallback needs to be exercised now or can wait.
close_reason:
Implemented WreqTransport (crates/twr-client/src/wreq_transport.rs) as the default HttpTransport impl: wreq 0.15.3 + wreq_util 0.1 (with the 'emulation' feature), Client::builder().emulation(Emulation::Chrome131).cookie_store(true).build(). CORRECTION to the plan (fixed in COMPREHENSIVEPLANFORTWITTERCLI.md): Emulation lives in the separate wreq-util crate, not wreq itself as originally written -- confirmed against docs.rs's official usage examples and cargo's real dependency resolution for this toolchain (wreq 0.16+ needs a newer rustc than installed here, so 0.15.3/wreq-util 0.1 is what actually resolves). A live spike test (chrome_emulation_reaches_a_neutral_fingerprint_checker, #[ignore] by default) hits tls.peet.ws/api/all -- a PUBLIC, NEUTRAL fingerprint-inspection service, deliberately NOT x.com, so no live X/Twitter request happens in this bead's scope (that's P0-4, gated behind a separate explicit step with real credentials).

TOOLCHAIN FINDING (significant, worth flagging beyond this bead): wreq's TLS impersonation links BoringSSL via the boring-sys build script, which requires cmake AND nasm as native build tools. Neither was present on this dev machine. Installed cmake successfully via winget (Kitware.CMake), which got the BoringSSL cmake configure step running, but it then failed requiring NASM (). winget reported 'Successfully installed' for NASM.NASM, but the binary is not resolvable afterward and No installed package found matching input criteria. reports 'No installed package found' -- i.e. the winget install silently did not actually complete/register, a real, reproducible environment gap on this box. Did not chase this further per explicit user direction to prioritize code+review over blocking on a full native build.

CONSEQUENCE: cargo build/test for crates/twr-client (and therefore the workspace as a whole) cannot currently link on this machine until nasm is properly installed (e.g. via choco install nasm, or a manual nasm.exe download added to PATH, then a fresh terminal session so Windows re-reads the updated PATH). This is a real, non-hypothetical instance of the plan's own risk #3 (wreq native-toolchain friction) -- worth documenting as a first-run setup step (or a CI-image concern) rather than assuming wreq 'just works' cross-platform.

WHAT WAS ACTUALLY VERIFIED without a full build: cargo fmt --all -- --check is clean on the new code (syntax-valid, well-formed Rust); the wreq/wreq-util dependency versions and feature flags were confirmed to resolve against the real crates.io index via cargo add --dry-run; the Emulation/ClientBuilder API surface was cross-checked against docs.rs's official current examples, not guessed.

NOT YET VERIFIED (carried forward, does not block moving on per user direction, but the P0 go/no-go decision bead must account for it): the actual live network round-trip against tls.peet.ws proving wreq's fingerprint is genuinely browser-shaped. Recommend: either fix the nasm install on a normal dev machine and re-run 'cargo test -p twr-client -- --ignored chrome_emulation_reaches_a_neutral_fingerprint_checker', or fall back to validating via the curl-impersonate-cli subprocess transport (plan's documented fallback, no BoringSSL linking needed) if native-toolchain friction turns out to be a recurring problem across contributor machines.

title: P0: rookie cross-platform cookie extraction spike (Windows/Linux/macOS)
description: Validate the 'rookie' crate can extract Chrome/Edge/Arc/Firefox/Brave cookies on all three OSes, with Windows treated as the primary risk: upstream issue #28 documents Chrome DB lock while Chrome is running, AES-GCM decryption failures on Chrome>=127, and misleading (non-Windows-specific) diagnostic messages in the Python original. Acceptance: confirm rookie extracts valid auth_token+ct0 on this Windows machine at minimum (macOS/Linux can be validated later in CI or by a contributor on that OS if unavailable here); if rookie fails the same way browser_cookie3 did, the mandatory fallback is the full-cookie-string paste path (plan SKILL.md Method C / plan §11 risk #1) — verify that path works as a safety net regardless of rookie's outcome.
close_reason: Created crates/twr-auth with the rookie crate (v0.5.6) as the browser-cookie backend and a manual cookie-string parser (parse_cookie_string/session_from_cookie_string) as the mandatory Method C fallback. extract_session_cookies() sweeps Chrome/Edge/Arc/Brave/Firefox in that order looking for x.com+twitter.com auth_token+ct0, stopping early on a complete pair; results surface only via a redacted ExtractionSummary (found/source/per-browser auth_token_present/ct0_present/error) -- raw cookie values are never logged, printed, or committed anywhere, matching the plan's failingInput redaction discipline (§5.3). WINDOWS RESULT (this machine, tested live via a non-ignored #[test], live_extraction_spike_on_this_machine): rookie did NOT find usable cookies -- Chrome and Edge both failed with 'Chrome cookies from version v130 can be decrypted only when running as admin due to appbound encryption!' (the exact upstream issue #28 failure mode: AES-GCM/app-bound decryption failing on Chrome>=127), Arc/Brave were not installed ('can't find cookies file'), Firefox likewise had no cookie DB on this machine. So on Windows, rookie alone is NOT sufficient without running as admin (or a future DPAPI/app-bound-decryption workaround) -- the manual cookie-paste fallback (Method C) is confirmed load-bearing, not just a nice-to-have. Method C is verified working via 4 unit tests with synthetic (non-real) cookie strings: parses semicolon-delimited name=value pairs, trims whitespace, and correctly reports auth_token/ct0 presence. Linux and macOS extraction paths compile (rookie's linux/macos backends are included via cfg) but are UNVERIFIED -- this machine is Windows-only, so those legs of the spike remain open per the bead's own acceptance criteria and should be validated in CI or by a contributor on that OS. cargo fmt --all -- --check clean; cargo build -p twr-auth and cargo test -p twr-auth (5/5 tests) pass. Full 'cargo build --workspace' currently fails on an unrelated, pre-existing issue: crates/twr-client's concurrent wreq/boringssl dependency (added by another agent's in-flight P0-1 work) requires cmake, which is not installed on this machine -- this is outside twr-auth's scope and untouched by this bead.

title: P0: port ClientTransaction derivation algorithm + Python vector parity
description: Port agentic-x/transaction.py's XClientTransaction algorithm into a standalone Rust function (this becomes the seed for the production twr-tx crate in P1, plan §7): fetch X's home page for verification metadata, parse the 4 loading-x-anim SVG frames plus ondemand.s indices, derive the per-request key (cubic/rotation/float-hex steps), base64-encode. Write a unit test asserting output parity against captured Python-generated vectors for at least one fixed input (same HTML snapshot in, same transaction ID out) — this is the single highest-uncertainty piece of reverse-engineered logic in the whole port and must be proven correct in isolation before anything depends on it. Only attach this header to GATED_OPS = {SearchTimeline, UserTweetsAndReplies, Followers} per upstream's documented behavior; other ops must NOT send it.
close_reason: Ported iSarabjitDhiman/XClientTransaction (via tmp/_research/agentic-x/src/agentic_x/transaction.py) verbatim into crates/twr-tx (math.rs: js_round/py_round_int/py_round2/float_to_hex/cubic_value/interpolate/rotation_matrix/solve/animate; frames.rs: lightweight HTML frame extractor mirroring _FrameParser; lib.rs: extract_verification_key/extract_key_byte_indices/compute_animation_key/generate_txid/ClientTransactionV1 implementing the RequestProof trait). TRUE cross-language parity achieved: ran the actual Python reference (after pip install platformdirs) with the exact synthetic page + monkeypatched time/random from agentic-x's tests/test_transaction.py, captured its output, and hardcoded those exact strings as Rust test assertions (compute_animation_key_matches_python_reference_exactly, generate_matches_python_reference_exactly) -- both pass, meaning the Rust port produces byte-for-byte identical output to the Python algorithm, not just internally self-consistent output. 15/15 unit tests pass (cargo test -p twr-tx), cargo fmt clean. This satisfies the bead's acceptance criterion in full. Remaining P0 work (P0-1 wreq live spike, P0-2 rookie cookie spike, P0-4 e2e call) requires live network/real X credentials which this bead's pure-logic scope deliberately did not need.

title: P0: end-to-end UserByScreenName call (wreq + rookie cookies + headers, no tx-id needed)
description: Combine P0-1's transport and P0-2's extracted cookies to make one real, successful UserByScreenName GraphQL call against x.com and parse a minimal user object out of the response (rest_id, screen_name, name). UserByScreenName is NOT a GATED_OP so this validates transport+auth+basic GraphQL request shape without yet depending on P0-3's transaction-ID work — keep P0-3 and P0-4 decoupled so a P0-3 delay doesn't block proving the core transport/auth story. DEFERRED (not closed, not abandoned): this needs a human to explicitly supply real X/Twitter session credentials (rookie could not extract usable cookies on the dev machine per the P0-2 bead's findings -- Method C manual paste, or running the browser as admin, are the only remaining paths) and a working native toolchain for crates/twr-client (see REMAINING.md). Making a live authenticated request to a real account is an outward-facing, account-risk action that should be a human's explicit choice, not something automatically attempted just because this bead is dependency-ready. See REMAINING.md for the exact unblock steps.

title: P0: Go/No-Go decision + write-up
description: Synthesize P0-1..P0-4 into an explicit GO or NO-GO decision, written down (as a close_reason on this bead is sufficient — no separate doc required). GO criteria: wreq gets a usable success rate against x.com (with curl-impersonate identified as available fallback if not), rookie extracts usable cookies on at least this dev machine, the transaction-ID port matches at least one Python-generated vector, and the P0-4 end-to-end call succeeds. If NO-GO on any hard blocker (e.g. wreq completely blocked AND curl-impersonate subprocess also fails), do not open any P1 bead — instead open a new bead documenting what alternative approach to investigate.

title: twr-error: finish ErrorKind/exit-code/suggestion/redaction contract
description: Extend the existing crates/twr-core error scaffold (already has ErrorKind + exit_code() + is_retryable() per plan §5.2's frozen 8-code table: 1 general/auth, 2 usage/policy, 3 not-found, 4 forbidden/rate-limited, 5 network, 6 contract-drift, 7 file-IO, 77 auth-required) with the full mapping table from plan §7's twr-error spec: 401/403->auth-required, 429/inner 88/348/349->forbidden/rate-limited, an HTTP 404 on the GraphQL endpoint itself->contract-drift, a 200 response whose payload is a tombstone/*Unavailable result->not-found (classify on PAYLOAD SHAPE not transport status, per plan §5.2's explicit disambiguation of the two different '404' meanings), 226->automated-behavior with fallback to the legacy statuses/update.json endpoint (bird's pattern). Also implement the failingInput redaction invariant (plan §5.3): flags whose values are secrets (--cookie/--auth-token/--ct0/--proxy-with-credentials) MUST be constructed pre-redacted as {flag, value:'[REDACTED]'} inside TwrError construction, never built from raw argv at a call site — this is a core protocol invariant (plan §0.1 #8), not optional. Unit tests: one per status/kind mapping, plus a redaction test asserting a --cookie value never survives serialization.
close_reason: Implemented full twr-error contract in crates/twr-core (commit 97cc135): status/api-code mapping, payload-shape 404 disambiguation, pre-redacted FailingInput, default suggestions, 12 tests green; clippy+fmt clean; pushed to main

title: CLI read commands: feed/bookmarks/search/tweet/show/article/list/user*
description: crates/twr, cli/ module. Implements the full read-command parity matrix from plan §1.1: feed [-t for-you|following] --cursor, bookmarks [folders [folder_id] [--since]], search [QUERY] with the full query-builder flags (-t Top|Latest|Photos|Videos, --from/--to/--lang/--since/--until, repeatable --has/--exclude, --min-likes/--min-retweets -- Latest search requires a transaction ID per twr-tx's GATED_OPS), tweet ID|URL (accepts a URL directly, normalizing to the numeric ID), show N (indexes into ~/.twr/last.json written after every list command -- out-of-range must be exit 3 not-found per plan §6, not exit 1), article ID|URL [--markdown] [--output file], list LIST_ID, user/user-posts/likes(own-account-only, noted in schema)/followers/following. Global read flags: -n/--max (respecting a CONFIGURABLE safety limit, default 200, never a hardcoded 500 -- this fixes upstream issue #50's pagination cap bug the right way: bounded-but-configurable, not literally unbounded), --input/-i, --output/-o, --filter (deferred to P3-FILTER if twr-filter isn't ready, but the flag should parse), --full-text, --json/--yaml. Blocked by twr-client (the actual network calls), twr-model (parsing), and twr-output (envelope rendering).
close_reason: Done in commit f4ebfaa: 12 read subcommands with full flag matrix, ID/URL normalization, last.json show-N (exit 3), search operator builder, exec layer over shared timeline loop, fast exit 77 (no rookie sweep in read path). title: twr-config: figment-based config resolution
description: crates/twr-config. Resolution order (plan §7): cwd config.yaml -> ~/.twr/config.yaml -> built-in defaults, deep-merged and normalized, with TWITTER_* env var overrides (figment's toml+env providers). Port the Python defaults exactly (plan §1.2 Config): fetch.count 50; filter topN/20/50 weights {likes:1.0, retweets:3.0, replies:2.0, bookmarks:5.0, views_log:0.5}; rateLimit {requestDelay:1.5, retries:3, backoff:5.0}. Fixes upstream issue #50's second bug: the Python original resolves its config path relative to the install directory (parent.parent lands inside site-packages under uv), which is wrong — twr must resolve strictly cwd-then-home, NEVER relative to the binary's own install location; add a regression test asserting this. 'twr config show' must mask any secret-shaped values.

title: twr-auth: full auth resolution chain + browser extraction + verify + login/logout
description: crates/twr-auth. Resolution order (plan §7): CLI flags -> env (TWITTER_AUTH_TOKEN+TWITTER_CT0) -> keyring/file (~/.twr/session) -> browser extraction via rookie (ordered by TWITTER_BROWSER env, TWITTER_CHROME_PROFILE for multi-profile Chrome). Verify via the verify_credentials->settings.json endpoint chain; on 401/403 attempt exactly one re-extraction before failing with exit 77. login refuses to silently overwrite a still-valid session (agent-x's pattern — logout first). Always keep the full-cookie-string paste fallback (Method C) available regardless of rookie's platform support. Addresses upstream issue #46 (unclear where to set credentials) via a 'twr login --guide' subcommand printing all three methods with doc links, and a first-run wizard triggered when twr status finds no session at all. Blocked by P0-2's rookie viability spike — if rookie doesn't work reliably, this bead's browser-extraction path needs a documented workaround before merging.
close_reason: Full chain in commit 2f117f8 (resolve/session/verify/guide modules, 16 new tests). Browser extraction from P0-2 kept as-is; verify HTTP chain belongs to twr-client (bead 3.3.7). 21/21 tests green, clippy+fmt clean, pushed.

title: twr-tx: production RequestProof trait + ClientTransactionV1 impl
description: crates/twr-tx. Promote P0-3's spike into the production abstraction from plan §3/§7: trait RequestProof { fn prepare(&self, op: Operation) -> Option<Proof> }, with ClientTransactionV1 as the current (and only) implementation — the trait boundary exists specifically so that if/when X changes or drops the transaction-ID requirement, only the impl swaps, no call site changes. Cache the derived key for 1h (transaction_cache.json), generate a FRESH single-use ID on every request (never replay), and attach it ONLY to GATED_OPS = {SearchTimeline, UserTweetsAndReplies, Followers} — every other GraphQL op must NOT carry this header. Unit tests re-assert the P0-3 vector parity plus the gated-vs-ungated attachment logic. Blocked by P0-3's algorithm spike being proven correct first.
close_reason: Production cache layer added in commit 2e59e8a (cache.rs: CachedIngredients, 1h TTL, load_fresh/store, 5 new tests). RequestProof trait + ClientTransactionV1 + GATED_OPS gating already in place from P0-3 with Python vector parity. 20/20 tests green, clippy+fmt clean, pushed to main.

title: twr-graphql: 4-layer query-ID resolver + bundle scraper + endpoints.yaml
description: crates/twr-graphql. Resolution order (plan §7): shipped baseline (the 22 FALLBACK_QUERY_IDS from plan §1.2, ported verbatim from Python's graphql.py) -> 24h disk cache (~/.twr/query-ids.json) -> an EXTRA rotation list of known-alternate IDs per op -> live rescrape (agentic-x's pattern: walk main.js plus up to 800 lazy chunks with 16 workers, a strict queryId/operationName/operationType regex). On an HTTP 404 from the GraphQL endpoint itself: invalidate that op's cached ID, trigger one refresh, retry once, then surface exit 6 (contract-drift) if still failing. TWR_QID_<OP> env vars let an operator pin an ID manually, bypassing all of the above for that op. endpoints.yaml holds per-op {queryId, features, toggles, rps, burst} read at RUNTIME (x-cli-vibe's data-driven pattern) so operators can hand-patch a stale ID without a rebuild. Also port the 21 FEATURES flags plus per-call extras from plan §1.2 verbatim (fetch_user's hidden/tipjar/subscriptions toggles, fetch_article's articles_preview_enabled, tweet_detail's withArticleRichContentState=True), stripping any false-valued feature to avoid HTTP 414.
close_reason: New crate twr-graphql in commit 3c4a83d: 4-layer resolver (env pin/disk/rotation/baseline), 24h qid cache, bundle scraper, runtime endpoints.yaml, 20 FEATURES + extras + 414 guard. 15/15 tests green, clippy+fmt clean, pushed.

title: twr-client: HttpTransport wiring + timeline loop + headers + token bucket
description: crates/twr-client. Wires P0-1's WreqTransport behind the HttpTransport trait (never call wreq directly outside this crate). Ports client.py's _fetch_timeline pagination loop: id dedup across pages, jittered requestDelay, count=min(remaining+5,40) per page, partial-resume on rate-limit. search/followers/following use POST per the Python original. Build the full header set from plan §1.2 verbatim (Bearer, Cookie, X-Csrf-Token, X-Twitter-Active-User, X-Twitter-Auth-Type, X-Twitter-Client-Language, OS-matched Chrome UA, Origin/Referer, dynamic sec-ch-ua*, Sec-Fetch-*, X-Client-Transaction-Id from twr-tx when gated). Exponential backoff on 429 (5s base x 3 retries per plan's rateLimit.backoff default). Respect TWITTER_PROXY. Implement the per-endpoint token bucket driven by endpoints.yaml's rps/burst fields (x-cli-vibe's pattern). Blocked by P0-1 (transport must be proven viable), P1-AUTH (needs resolved cookies), P1-GRAPHQL (needs resolved query IDs/features), and P1-TX (needs the transaction-proof trait for gated ops).
close_reason: Wired in commit 5c26826: headers.rs (_build_headers port), throttle.rs (token bucket + page/jitter math), timeline.rs (_fetch_timeline loop with truncated resume + backoff). 18/18 tests green, clippy+fmt clean, pushed. Live e2e stays in P0-4 (needs real creds).

title: Introspection commands: schema, commands, doctor, status, query-ids
description: All fully offline (no network/auth required except status): 'twr schema [--json]' dumps JSON Schema per envelope type. 'twr commands [--json]' catalogs every command's args/flags/policy-level/idempotency/examples so an agent never needs external docs. 'twr doctor [--refresh] [--json]' runs 7 INDEPENDENT checks per plan §5.4 -- QUERY_ID, FEATURES, TOGGLES, TX_ID, AUTH, RESPONSE_SHAPE, TLS -- each reporting {check,status,suggestion}; critically, a correct query ID with a failing parser must report as a RESPONSE_SHAPE failure, NOT get conflated with QUERY_ID (refreshing the query ID will not fix a response-shape mismatch, and doctor must say so explicitly -- this was a specifically reviewed and locked design decision, do not regress it). 'twr status [--json]' is the auth gate every workflow should call first: {authenticated, user?, cookieSource}, exit 77 if not authenticated -- addresses upstream issue #46 by clearly distinguishing 'no cookies' vs 'expired (401/403)' vs 'partial env-only auth (226 risk)'. 'twr query-ids [--fresh] [--json]' inspects/refreshes the twr-graphql cache. Blocked by twr-output (envelope), twr-graphql (query-id state to report on), twr-auth (auth state to report on), twr-tx (tx-key freshness to report on). Also addresses upstream issue #45 (closed, but a transparency complaint worth not regressing): the Python original's transaction-ID generation is a black box behind an external xclienttransaction library with no in-repo explanation, which is exactly the question issue #45's reporter asked and never really got answered. twr must NOT repeat that: add 'twr doctor --explain-tx' printing the twr-tx derivation steps (verification-meta fetch, SVG frame parse, key derivation) in human-readable form, since the algorithm itself lives in-repo (crates/twr-tx) rather than an opaque external dependency.

title: Phase P2 — Writes + media + safety hardening
description: Plan §9 P2. Ships every write command (post/reply/quote/delete/like/unlike/retweet/unretweet/bookmark/unbookmark/follow/unfollow) wired through the uniform --apply/--dry-run/--no-interactive decision table (plan §5.3 — this applies to EVERY write, not just delete/follow, per the reviewed and locked design), the idempotency state machine (plan §5.5: prepared/sent/acknowledged/unknown — client-side best-effort dedup, explicitly NOT server-side exactly-once, unknown state never auto-retries), media upload (raw-binary multipart + chunked GIF to 15MB per closed upstream PR #41, optional --compress via the image crate), and --policy gating. Acceptance, stated as the state machine actually guarantees rather than an unverifiable exactly-once claim: an acknowledged idempotency key returns the cached result instead of resubmitting (no duplicate client-initiated POST); an unknown-state key never auto-retries; read_only policy blocks every write with exit 2; every write without --apply produces a dry_run envelope and touches the network zero times.

title: Implement §5.3 --apply/--dry-run/--no-interactive decision table
description: The uniform write-safety mechanism (plan §5.3, locked after review -- applies to EVERY write command, not just delete/follow). Exact 5-row truth table to implement: (--apply=no,--dry-run=no,TTY)->prompt for confirmation, yes->execute / no-or-EOF->exit 0 with a dry_run-shaped cancellation note; (--apply=no,--dry-run=no,--no-interactive)->exit 2 usage/policy-denied, the call is ambiguous by design and an agent must say which it wants; (--apply=no,--dry-run=yes,either)->run the DryRun preview {dry_run:true, operation, validation:'passed'} (NEVER 'would_succeed' -- no guarantee a later real call succeeds, this exact wording was specifically reviewed and locked), exit 0, network untouched; (--apply=yes,--dry-run=no,either)->execute for real; (--apply=yes,--dry-run=yes,either)->exit 2, mutually exclusive flags is a usage error. This is foundational -- every write command bead below depends on it.
close_reason: Done in commit fb0a305: twr-core/apply.rs 5-row table + unit tests, --apply/--dry-run/--no-interactive root flags (env TWR_*), decide() wired in main. Write commands branch on it in 3.4.3/3.4.4. twr-core 25 + twr 5 green, pushed.

title: Idempotency state machine (prepared/sent/acknowledged/unknown)
description: Plan §5.5, a specifically reviewed and corrected design (an earlier draft over-claimed 'never double-posts', which was flagged as impossible to guarantee against an unofficial API with no native idempotency contract -- the FIXED, accurate acceptance is: client-side best-effort retry deduplication, NOT server-side exactly-once). --idempotency-key stored in ~/.twr/idempotency.json for 24h. States: prepared (request built, not sent) -> sent (in flight) -> acknowledged (server responded with success, result cached) | unknown (timeout/network failure after sending, genuinely no way to know if the server received it). On unknown: NEVER auto-retry -- return an envelope explicitly reporting the unknown state with a suggestion to check manually. On acknowledged + same key: return the cached result instead of resubmitting -- this dedups only within this LOCAL state, it does not and cannot prove the server saw exactly one request server-side. Blocked by P2-DECISION since idempotency only matters on the --apply=yes execution path.
close_reason: Done in commit d57d992: twr-core/idempotency.rs (24h store, pre_check 3-way, prune-on-load, 2 tests). Consumed by write commands in 3.4.3. twr-core 27 green, pushed.

title: Media upload: raw-binary multipart + chunked GIF (PR #41 pattern)
description: upload.rs in twr-client. INIT->APPEND->FINALIZE flow against upload.twitter.com/i/media/upload.json, limit <=5MB for jpeg/png/gif/webp per the Python original, PLUS the closed-but-never-merged upstream PR #41's improvements which this port adopts directly: chunked GIF upload up to 15MB via media_category=tweet_gif with 1MB APPEND chunks, and raw-binary multipart instead of base64 encoding (roughly a third less transfer overhead). --compress N is an optional dependency on the image crate re-encoding JPEG/PNG/WebP before upload (never applied to GIFs). Blocked by P2-POST since media only attaches to post/reply/quote. This bead is the cookie-backend half of upstream issue #13's video-upload request (open) -- the official-API half (chunked video via the v2 media endpoints) is separately tracked in the P4 video bead, since issue #13's original scope predates PR #31's api-v2 work and this port intentionally splits the two backends.

title: Policy gating: --policy read_only/engagement/write
description: Root flag enforced across every write command from P2-POST and P2-ACTIONS: read_only blocks ALL writes (exit 2); engagement permits like/retweet/follow/bookmark but blocks post/delete; write (the default) permits everything else already gated by --apply. This must be checked BEFORE the --apply/--dry-run decision table so a read_only-scoped agent task structurally cannot post even with --apply passed.

title: Write safety: delay jitter, daily mutation budget, delete preview
description: Preserve the Python original's write-delay behavior: 1.5-4s random jitter as a floor between write operations that a caller cannot tune below (only raise). A configurable daily mutation budget, default 200 (x-cli-vibe's pattern) -- this is an explicit LOCAL SAFETY POLICY independent of and making no claim about X's actual server-side rate limit (plan §5.5's specific correction of an earlier draft that conflated the two); exceeding it exits 2 with a suggestion, and it's configurable upward but never fully disableable.

Cursor-based sync_state per channel/user/search-query analogous to discord-db's per-channel cursors.
